audience.programmeDescription: University College Venlo is an English-taught liberal arts and sciences bachelor focused on sustainable food systems. It examines how food is produced, how people make choices and how food affects health and the environment.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR plans illustrate three related directions. The Venlo example follows the named modules in the regulations and catalogue. It includes the 2.5 EC final-year Portfolio separately from the 20 EC of introductory skills and projects, since the regulations give different totals in their summary and module list.

cellNotes.text: Both develop academic inquiry, including evaluating sources and framing research questions. UCR also covers personal development and community engagement.
Both develop research design and measurement. UCR also teaches descriptive and inferential statistics in this course.
Both examine evidence and the reliability of claims. UCR focuses on misinformation and misleading reasoning, while Venlo examines how knowledge and evidence inform decisions under uncertainty.
Both develop team research and the reporting of findings. UCR focuses on qualitative research. Venlo completes a linked research sequence with data analysis in R, an article and a poster.
Both develop data analysis skills. Venlo collects and analyses data within an ongoing group project, while UCR studies experimental design and multivariate statistics.
Venlo begins a supervised research project with a group proposal. UCR develops research planning within methods courses.
Venlo’s final-year Portfolio follows development across the degree. UCR’s Personal & Professional Development course is taken in Year 1.
Both examine how the body functions, including digestion and metabolism. Venlo gives greater attention to nutrition and macronutrients.
Both examine judgement, incentives and biases. Venlo applies the material to questions of food choice, health and sustainability.
Both examine sustainability challenges and connections between society and environmental change. UCR focuses on climate drivers, impacts and responses.
Both take a whole-system view of environmental effects. UCR uses life-cycle assessment, while Venlo models interactions within food systems.
The example uses 15 EC outside a single concentration, including humanities and the alternate concentration. Interdisciplinary curricula instead require 10 EC of humanities.
The example uses 75 EC of concentration courses. The concentration requires at least 20 EC of advanced coursework and allows at most 20 EC of introductory coursework.
Choose five intermediate or advanced skills trainings.
Choose three concentration projects, including at least one advanced project.
Venlo requires a 20 EC Capstone after at least 140 EC. UCR’s 15 EC optional independent research is shown separately from the scheduled courses.

notes.text: Venlo brings together behaviour, health and responsible innovation around food systems. The UCR plans offer related perspectives through farming and sustainability, human biology and public health, or psychology and consumer research.

Venlo offers specialist courses in nutrition, food processing and safety, sensory science and food product development. The UCR plans cover related topics through broader courses. Venlo also requires a 20 EC Capstone.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENECON111.text: Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.

BENECON212.text: Study how consumers and producers make decisions under scarcity. Explore key concepts such as rational choice, decision-making under uncertainty, and non-egoistic preferences. Analyze market structures, strategic interactions, and factor markets. Learn how markets function and examine the impact of regulation. Develop analytical tools to better understand behavior and engage with empirical research.

BENECON311.text: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.

BENECON314.name: Behavioral Economics
BENECON314.text: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.

BENENTR111.name: Consumer Product Design
BENENTR111.text: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.

BENENTR211.name: Marketing & Consumer Engagement
BENENTR211.text: Marketing & Consumer Engagement examines consumer psychology, marketing strategy, responsible brand development and customer engagement. Students analyse a company strategy, design a brand and investigate a consumer phenomenon using academic literature and primary and secondary evidence. Digital marketing and customer-journey mapping connect analysis with practical recommendations.

BENENTR311.text: See how companies figure out what customers love and what they don’t. You’ll plan and carry out real research, analyze what you find, and share your results. Our course shows you how to gather opinions and turn them into smart business ideas—perfect for future marketers, analysts, or entrepreneurs.

BENENTR312.text: Examines how trade, globalisation and political, cultural and technological conditions shape international business decisions. Students analyse governance, responsibility and trade-policy conflicts, investigate a business question, and develop an evidence-based market-entry strategy. A tariff case applies game theory to stakeholder choices.

ENSDELT312.name: Governance of Sustainability
ENSDELT312.text: This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.
